newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian businessman stands firm on gold find.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian businessman stands firm on gold find.

text.p: Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh said on Tuesday he had no intention of giving up his claim to a major share of the Busang gold find despite the entry of President Suharto's eldest son into the arena.
Merukh has been locked in a dispute with Busang's majority owner, Canadian firm Bre-X Minerals Ltd, over his claim to a 40 percent share in the spectacular find in Indonesia's Kalimantan province.
"There is no change in my position. I will pursue my claim for 40 percent (of Busang)," Merukh told Reuters.

Bre-X announced on Monday in Toronto that it had entered into an alliance with PT Panutan Duta of the Panutan Group run by Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto. The group has interests in energy, mining and telecommunications.

Bre-X said PT Panutan would receive $40 million over 40 months plus a 10 percent interest in the richest parts of the Busang property in return for acting as consultant and helping the Alberta-based company deal with technical and administrative matters.
There was no comment on Merukh's statement from Bre-X's Jakarta office, which routinely passes all queries to Toronto.

An industry analyst, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the link-up was expected to clear the way for the government to sign contracts of work with Bre-X which the company needs to continue exploration and development of its property.
Analysts said Sigit's Panutan Group had applied for gold concessions from the government in the past, but added that the company was not considered a major player in the sector.
Despite Bre-X's tie-up Merukh said he would continue his claim to 40 percent of the Busang claim, one of the world's richest with estimated reserves of at least 47 million ounces.
Analysts predicted however that Merukh could come under heavy pressure for a quick settlement with Bre-X.

The dispute has so far led the Indonesian government to delay the signing of contracts of work with Bre-X for the exploration of Blocks II and III -- the richest areas of the Busang site -- until the dispute is resolved.
Merukh says he controls 20 percent of Block I through two of his companies, PT Krueng Gasui and PT Sungai Atan Perdana.

He claims a 20-percent interest in Blocks II and III through his former partnership with Westralian Resource Project, which sold its interest to Waverly Finance Management of Scotland, which in turn sold the interest to Bre-X.
Merukh says he has options to buy a further 20 percent in the find.
